title: Crop Repeated Headers Before Stitching Screenshots
description: Crop fixed headers and overlapping content before joining iPhone screenshots. Use one shared landmark to check that the join keeps every line once.
direct: Crop away the repeated header and use one shared line to decide where each screenshot ends. Then stack the cropped screenshots in reading order.
figureAlt: Two paper mockups of overlapping screen captures with crop marks where one repeated row should be removed.
figureCaption: AI mockups show how to keep a shared row once at a join.
cards.decision.heading: Pick a line you can find twice
cards.decision.body: In two overlapping screenshots, find a distinctive sentence, message or list item. Keep it at the end of the first image. Start the second image just below it.
sections.detail-1.heading: Keep the next capture easy to join
sections.detail-1.body: When you take new screenshots, scroll far enough to show new content but keep a few lines from the earlier image. Hold the phone orientation and text size steady. Choose an item that appears only once as your landmark.
sections.detail-2.heading: Check the shared copy
sections.detail-2.body: Space Sheep Studio develops Combine Photos for iPhone. The app arranges screenshots in one image. The manual crops do the overlap removal. Check the final file at the size your reader will see and remove private information before sharing.

steps.step-1.text: Duplicate the captures if you want separate working copies. In Photos, crop the fixed header or footer from each image where it repeats. Leave the first header if it tells the reader what the screen is about.
steps.step-2.text: Crop the join at a gap between two lines. Check that the first screenshot ends on the last complete line you want to keep and the second starts on the next one. Use the same left and right edges.
steps.step-3.text: Place the crops in order in the vertical layout in Combine Photos: Stitch & Grid. Export one image. Zoom in on the join and check that no line repeats or disappears.
